metadata.title: Massive Bhog Making at Delhi’s Oldest Durga Pujo
metadata.description:
Kashmere Gate Durga Puja, fondly known as DDPCCS, is more than just an annual celebration; it is a living legacy of devotion, tradition, and community. Celebrating its 115th year, this puja is one of Delhi’s oldest and most iconic, hosted at the historic Bengali Senior Secondary School. Renowned for its vibrant festivities, cultural richness, and the grand-scale distribution of bhog, it continues to bring people together, fostering a deep sense of belonging and joy.

On Saptami eve this year, we immersed ourselves in the festive spirit of this iconic puja and witnessed the fascinating process behind the preparation of bhog, which is served to thousands of devotees visiting the pandal.

Here, we met Sudipto, who warmly guided us through this extraordinary experience. Our journey began with the serene ritual of pushpanjali (flower offerings), setting the tone for the day. From there, we headed to the bustling makeshift arena where the bhog-making process was unfolding. The sight was mesmerizing: massive cauldrons bubbling with fragrant ingredients, volunteers moving swiftly, and a seamless choreography of tasks creating an atmosphere of devotion and dedication.

We learned from the members that the main bhog khichuri—a porridge-like dish made of rice, dal, and vegetables—was prepared in the kitchen by a team of special cooks. This was then combined with labra, a flavorful mixed vegetable dish cooked separately, and tempered with whole spices to enhance the aroma. Meanwhile, other elements of the meal were being cooked in large quantities at the makeshift setup.

Under the expert supervision of the head chef, the team coordinated every step flawlessly, ensuring that the meal was ready in record time. Watching this intricate operation unfold was both humbling and inspiring, showcasing the power of community and teamwork.

As the final dishes were prepared and combined, we delved deeper into the rich history of this puja and its enduring legacy. The devotion and love behind every aspect of this celebration were palpable.

Finally, we sat down to savor the bhog—a meal that was as divine in taste as it was in spirit. Simple yet soul-satisfying, it carried the essence of the goddess’s blessings and the collective efforts of the community.

Our visit to the Kashmere Gate Durga Puja was more than just a glimpse into a celebration; it was an experience of unity, devotion, and heritage, leaving us in awe of its grandeur and warmth.
